cohort: The study included nulliparous women at term with a single fetus in cephalic presentation and spontaneous onset of labor (Robson Group 1) who received care in a new birthing room designed to promote person-centredness.
finding: Childbirth outcomes, including mode of birth and childbirth experience, were comparable between women with rape-related pregnancies and other pregnant women when care was provided in a birthing room designed to promote person-centred care.
mod_finding: No statistically significant differences were observed in vaginal birth rates (81.8% vs 83.4%) or Caesarean section rates (18.2% vs 16.6%) between women with rape-related pregnancies and the comparison group.
